---
title: "From source geometry to a solver model"
description: "Understand occurrences, Entities, Nets, regions and the distinction between declared and observed geometry."
scgsim-kind: "concept"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/concepts/geometry"
---

A component describes local geometry. Placing it twice creates two occurrences
of those facts; it does not rename the component's own local Entities. A named
occurrence path qualifies identity before flattening, so two touching polygons
can still retain separate source lineage. The final study then assigns those
qualified Entities to Nets. Neither touching appearance nor similar labels
performs that assignment.

For example, `chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD` names one source Entity in one named
placement. `xmon_pad` is its final Net in the Xmon study. Eight sibling bump
Entities can belong to `Ground` while remaining eight source members. A backend
may aggregate them into a computational physical group; the group serves mesh
or integral work and is not a ninth Entity or a promise of eight raw results.

The PDK owns material, fabrication level and Z/thickness facts. The component
owns local polygons, ports and topology selectors. The study's GeometryPlan
owns occurrence names and the final Net map. Preparing the plan produces one
immutable snapshot for backend consumption. The exact API, assignment errors,
array handling and snapshot schema live in the
[GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd).

## A region is part of the model

The outer vacuum envelope is an explicit source input on the plan. It encloses
the study and is partitioned around modeled bodies. An authored inter-die gap
remains distinct from that outer region. Changing padding changes the physical
model rather than merely the camera view, so prepare a new snapshot when the
source envelope changes.

Shared input does not imply identical exterior conditions. Palace's unspecified
Eigenmode exterior has its natural PMC condition; the current AEDT EPR Region
uses HFSS's default Perfect E policy. Record the envelope and boundary choices
when comparing models. No implicit conversion makes those experiments equal.

## Route A and Route B answer different approximation questions

Route A represents face metal by zero-thickness PEC sheets, with the explicit
supported face/profile assumptions. Route B constructs finite metal and uses
its closed exterior PEC shell; Palace excludes the conductor interior from its
solution tetrahedra. Finite source dimensions, PEC approximation and native CAD
implementation are separate facts. A Route-A profile may preserve physical
substrate-face coordinates or explicitly normalize a two-face gap; it is not an
automatic fallback when Route B is hard to mesh.

A surface interface needs material-side and contact evidence, not just a name
such as MA or MS. Local support can vary over one sheet; substrate holes and
exposed portions retain their own meaning. The contract records that detail so
loss analysis can state which patches were evaluated and which were not.

## Read evidence at the stage that produced it

| Stage | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Source summary | Normalized declared inputs, source identity and unknowns |
| Prepared catalogue/config | Planned backend selections and approximation choices |
| Bound mesh/native readback | Geometry and assignments observed in that backend |
| Returned solve receipt and outputs | Recorded execution and actual returned result evidence |
| Report/plot | A presentation of the selected evidence and assumptions |

A preview cannot create a missing Net or prove field accuracy. A completed
receipt cannot create an uncomputed sidewall contribution. Retaining stage and
source identity keeps these observations useful without promoting them into a
stronger claim. Return to the [course map](../examples.qmd), or read
[implementation responsibilities](../architecture.qmd) after completing the
workflow.
